articles.title: Coach Prime's honeymoon phase is over and the luster is gone. Colorado needs to win now
articles.summary: Deion Sanders' record at Colorado isn't great and he can't really ride on his shine from previous years anymore. The Buffaloes need to win this season.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — On Thursday night, Deion Sanders will start his fourth season as Colorado's football coach. And now we will finally get to judge him for exactly that.

Not as the ratings machine who drew sold-out crowds and celebrities to the sideline in Boulder. Not as a soundbite promising to do things that sounded good but were impossible to deliver. Not as a reality show or a cancer patient who, amidst a genuine health crisis, parlayed his diagnosis into an endorsement deal in the way only Coach Prime could pull off.

Now, in Year 4, he's just a football coach running a football program that needs to win some games and win them soon.

"We better win," Sanders said at Big 12 media days. "We're going to win. I love what I got. I love what I see."

And the rest of us? Well, we'll start to see when Sanders returns to a city where he was once an icon, bringing his team to Georgia Tech.

Sanders' relationship with Atlanta is a delicious subplot, of course. In 1989, the Atlanta Falcons drafted him No. 5 overall and he immediately became a huge star as one of the NFL's best cornerbacks and a centerfielder who played 292 games for the Atlanta Braves.

But the era of Prime nostalgia has less to do with his current situation than it ever has.

All the excitement around Sanders' first two seasons at Colorado, when his team was a true phenomenon that broke through the college football bubble and into the mainstream culture? It's gone.

The players like Travis Hunter and his son, Shedeur Sanders, who carried Colorado to nine wins in 2024 despite a deeply flawed roster? They're in the NFL.

The recruiting momentum that had Colorado competing for players who never would have otherwise considered going to Boulder? It seems to be in the rear-view mirror.

Colorado went 3-9 last season and won just a single game in the Big 12. Sanders changed out much of his staff, including both coordinators. Just like every other coach, Sanders in Year 4 no longer gets graded on a curve. The attention he's bringing off the field no longer matters. It's time to produce.

"I'm thankful that God didn't allow my neck to go back and look all the way back, because that would be a tremendous pain right now," Sanders said. "I'm thankful that I look ahead, and I'm right on point. I'm loving everything that we've added. I'm loving what we did in the portal. I'm loving what we're doing recruiting-wise right now. We're right where we want to be. Right where we want to be. We're going to even get better."

If you could win national titles through sheer force of optimism and willpower, Sanders would already have a coaching career minted for the Hall of Fame. He wouldn't be Prime if he wasn't constantly selling, constantly promising, constantly painting the rosiest picture of what he sees regardless of what the rest of us see.

But suffice it to say, the college football world is skeptical about whether he can deliver. Though nobody expects Colorado to fire Sanders in the traditional sense, many industry insiders have their eye on Boulder as a place where both sides could decide they've had enough of this marriage if it results in another losing season.

Sanders, however, is not the type to just give up. Though everything about the way he does the job is non-traditional (including how much time he spends at his ranch in Texas rather than on campus), give him this much: He's still trying.

Colorado once again overhauled its roster with more than 40 transfers, many of them from power conference programs. The Buffaloes completely changed their offense by hiring Brennan Marion and his "Go-Go" scheme away from a head coaching job at Sacramento State. They are truly starting from scratch on defense after giving up a Big 12-worst 425 yards per game last year, with former Virginia Tech coordinator Chris Marve overseeing a transfer-heavy unit.

Colorado might have more talent top to bottom than it did in Sanders' first two seasons, albeit without the star power that Hunter and Shedeur Sanders brought to the field. It was also a huge win that quarterback Julian Lewis, a former blue-chip recruit, decided not to enter the transfer portal after a freshman season in which he played just four games to preserve his redshirt.

"I want to see how we get to the ball defensively because Marve has them flying to the ball," Sanders said at a press conference this week. "I want to see the explosiveness of some of the backs we have because we've been seeing it. Our offensive linemen are doing a wonderful job doing in the run as well as the pass game and making the quick decisions to get the ball to these playmakers. We've got some guys that are really fast, man. They can go. They can change the dynamics of a game instantaneously, we have to get the ball to them and let them do what they do. So I'm excited."

Though most prognosticators have pegged Colorado for a lower-tier finish in the Big 12, it feels like one of those teams that we know almost nothing about. When the Buffs debut Thursday, we should be ready for anything.

But how many people are even paying attention anymore?

When Sanders arrived at Colorado and instantly brought fans to the stadium and money to the NIL fun and insane TV ratings, instantly reviving a program that had been dormant for years, you could squint and see the pathway to longstanding national relevance.

In some ways, though, Sanders was probably better equipped to win big in the pre-NIL era where his fame was more useful in recruiting. After all, the man got Hunter — a Heisman winner — to initially enroll at Jackson State. You could argue that nobody in the history of college football has out-recruited the reputation of their school than Sanders for a period of time.

That's harder to do when recruiting is a money race that Colorado, by and large, cannot win.

It leads to the existential question of this season: If Sanders is no longer dominating the zeitgeist and his celebrity is no longer a major edge in recruiting, what value is he bringing as a college head coach?

It can only be in the winning. He has not done enough of it yet. Thursday night starts a new season, but more importantly, a chance to change the narrative.

"It's gonna be a tremendous challenge but I love it," he said. "I absolutely love it."

images.caption: Deion Sanders is 16-21 as the head coach at Colorado. (Matthew Jonas/Getty Images) (Matthew Jonas/Boulder Daily Camera via Getty Images via Getty Images)

articles.title: Hasta 15 jugadores se han negado a fichar por el Ceuta por la crisis en la ciudad
articles.standfirst: El presidente del club desveló que la situación ha provocado que varios futbolistas hayan cambiado de opinión, pese a tener casi cerrado su acuerdo con el club
articles.summary: El presidente del club desveló que la situación ha provocado que varios futbolistas hayan cambiado de opinión, pese a tener casi cerrado su acuerdo con el club
articles.body: El presidente del Ceuta, Luhay Hamido, expuso este jueves los problemas que ha encontrado su equipo para configurar su plantilla debido a la crisis por la llegada masiva de inmigrantes y reconoció que "hasta 15 jugadores dijeron que no" al equipo, pese a tener casi cerrado su acuerdo con el club, por la situación que atraviesa la ciudad autónoma. "A la mujer le da miedo, a los niños... Se entiende por la información que te llega. Si no lo estás viviendo, pues parece un estado de sitio", dijo en declaraciones a la Cadena Ser. Luhay Hamido reconoció que en un mes "ha cambiado la situación en la ciudad" porque estaba "bien a nivel de turismo, económico o deportivo". Y añadió que "el Ceuta es más que un club: convivimos cuatro culturas y nos abrazamos todos, se ha convertido en un templo y el equipo se ha convertido en un denominador común muy potente", explicó. "Los jugadores y el míster tienen familia e hijos. Ven a la ciudad que no es la que ellos conocen y eso les afecta, pero entrenan con normalidad. Esto es segura y la Policía está haciendo un gran trabajo", explicó Luhay, que matizó que el club incluso ofreció a los jugadores la posibilidad de conocer personalmente la ciudad antes de tomar una decisión definitiva. "Les invitamos a que viniesen a verla sin compromiso alguno, a ver las instalaciones, cómo trabajábamos... y el último día conseguimos fichajes. Creo que vamos a competir con esta plantilla. No somos de ponernos nerviosos y de ser resultadistas. Nosotros tratamos de blindar a los jugadores y meterlos en una burbuja", añadió.

images.caption: Los jugadores caballas, con una camiseta donde se lee "Ceuta no se vende, Ceuta se defiende"

articles.title: SEC Sues LSU, Alleging a Coordinated Push to Recruit Ex-Pro Athletes in Defiance of Rules
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — The Southeastern Conference filed a lawsuit against LSU and its leadership in Alabama federal court on Thursday, alleging the school had "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes" against league rules.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — The Southeastern Conference filed a lawsuit against LSU and its leadership in Alabama federal court on Thursday, alleging the school had "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes" against league rules.

The extraordinary court filing against one of the league's founding members in 1933 seeks an injunction barring LSU from violating the SEC's First Amendment rights by forcing it to "associate with conduct that is contrary to the conference's purpose and mission." It was filed in Alabama because the SEC is based in Birmingham.

The lawsuit was made public as SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey testified 400 miles away in a Baton Rouge courtroom not far from Tiger Stadium, defending the league's authority to enforce its week-old rules barring former pros from returning to play at its 16 member schools. Former New Orleans Saints defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright, two players who hope to suit up for LSU, sat next to each other in the gallery as the hearing began.

Sankey took the stand to explain that SEC member presidents and chancellors felt that they needed to establish a line between professional and college sports and that there needed to be ways to hold schools accountable.

"The line between professional sports and college sports needs to be maintained," Sankey testified, adding that the league was concerned about incoming athletes being displaced from limited roster spots.

In their questioning of Sankey, attorneys for the athletes cited numerous examples of when SEC eligibility rules align with NCAA rules, suggesting the potential of illegal collusion. They questioned why league members met last week to adopt stiff penalties for the very actions addressed in the Louisiana state court's temporary injunction against the NCAA.

The attorneys also asked why the SEC singled out players who signed contracts with specific U.S.-based leagues — the NFL, NBA and WNBA — but not overseas pro leagues or women's pro soccer leagues. When Sankey tried to qualify an answer about whether the SEC had previously punished a member school for adding a player with previous pro experience, plaintiffs' attorney Tony Clayton said, "I didn't ask how to build a clock. I'm just asking what time it is."

Sankey acknowledged that there had previously been no such punishment, but that it had been considered against Alabama last basketball season when the Crimson Tide briefly played a former G-League player.

East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden scheduled the hearing concerning the status of his temporary injunction preventing the NCAA from ruling recent former pros or fifth-year college athletes ineligible, a stance also taken by the SEC and other Power Four conferences with formal rules adopted last week.

Jorden also wanted the NCAA to explain why it should not be held in contempt after the power conferences set up potential punishments of its member schools who place former NFL or NBA athletes on their football or basketball rosters.

There was no indication when Jorden might rule but the football season is already underway and most teams playing this weekend, including 11th-ranked LSU. The SEC requires its schools to submit final 2026 rosters for the season by Friday.

Players going to court has become common

The players in question also include former Denver Broncos defensive back Blake Cotton, who like Harris and Wright is hoping to join LSU and new coach Lane Kiffin .

Wright, who played for Kiffin last season at Mississippi, started practicing at LSU this week, too late to be eligible for Saturday's home opener against Clemson under the NCAA's required seven days of practice. Harris, who also played at Ole Miss last season, has committed to LSU, while Cotton, who played at Utah last fall, has been recruited by Kiffin.

All three are among a host of athletes who've argued in lawsuits around the country that they are unfairly being denied an opportunity to spend a fifth year in college under newly adopted NCAA rules allowing for five full years of competition. In all, the NCAA says there are approximately 450 athlete plaintiffs seeking additional eligibility through litigation, with some 300 of them winning the ability to play at least for now and about 150 who have been rejected.

The athletes in the case who signed pro contracts have argued they did so only because current rules that would have allowed them another college season weren't adopted until after their decisions to leave for the chance to make an NFL roster.

The SEC filed a brief in the case on Wednesday in which it stated that the question before the judge should be a narrow one regarding whether the conference "can enforce and require its member institutions to comply with SEC rules." The SEC's proposed punishments include significant fines, up to half-season suspensions for coaches and member universities' loss of voting privileges on league business matters.

Sankey provided an affidavit stating that SEC university presidents had voted 15-0 in favor of the new rules, with LSU's Wade Rousse abstaining. Sankey also said the SEC was acting on its own and not attempting to collude with the NCAA to stop Kiffin from bringing in ex-pros.

The fight over eligibility between schools and their own conferences and the NCAA has simmered for months and spilled into politics.

Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr reportedly sent a letter of support to Sankey, encouraging him to take "all measures available" to punish LSU if it added former NFL players. Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill, who attended the hearing and chatted with plaintiffs' attorneys before the proceeding, countered in a brief that the NCAA had subjected athletes in the case to a "classic bait-and-switch."

articles.title: Fifa accuses Uefa of 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: The governing bodies have traded blows since Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
articles.body:
Fifa has accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to litigation over president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Last week European football's governing body filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa as part of potential criminal claims in Switzerland.

In a dramatic escalation of the controversy, Uefa accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" and "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by [him] for his own benefit" over the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

However, world governing body Fifa has now responded with court filings lodged in the US - and seen by the BBC - requesting that permission for access to documents be deferred, or opposed by the end of the month.

Fifa claims Uefa's argument "suffers from a fundamental defect" and "legal deficiencies".

"Uefa seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that Uefa admittedly lacks the authority to initiate. Despite that threshold problem, Uefa asks this court to authorise sweeping discovery about the FFE."

It said it had "made clear" that the creation of FFE was "only a proposal", adding that it could have only proceeded on the condition that the majority of member associations supported it and "the relevant approvals of the Fifa Council".

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, Uefa issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership," it wrote in the court filing.

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

It also claimed that Uefa's "economic motivation" was to prevent smaller countries from having the "financial strength to compete with the European elite".

"If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces Uefa's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments," Fifa said.

"By raising funds to allow some of Fifa's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad."

Uefa has declined to comment, although BBC Sport has been told insiders believe that if Fifa has nothing to hide, it should disclose the documents and speed up the legal process. It has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down from three confederations.

Uefa has also asked a court in New York to approve a legal document ordering testimony and documents from venture capitalist Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, who was set to be the lead investor in FFE, and his company Thrive Eternal.

Thrive had held talks with Infantino about heading up a $4.2bn (£3.1bn) investment in 20% of a new Fifa commercial subsidiary, before the idea was abandoned days after it was revealed in July amid a huge backlash.

At the time, Fifa claimed FFE would have increased the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle from £5.9m to £14.7m.

On Sunday, Kushner expressed regret over FFE, saying: "While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to… had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

Uefa has also asked for the disclosure of documents from American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed".

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at about £15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". Uefa claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

images.caption: Image caption, Gianni Infantino became Fifa president in 2016

articles.title: Las lesiones castigan al Alba
articles.standfirst: La enfermería manchega sigue llenándose en un inicio liguero preocupante
articles.summary: La enfermería manchega sigue llenándose en un inicio liguero preocupante
articles.body: El Albacete tiene un problema con las lesiones. Tres jornadas de Liga y cinco nuevas bajas se suman a un problema que ya le marcó negativamente la pasada campaña. Alberto González está obligado a reinventar su libreto cada jornada, mientras pierde efectivos y las dudas se expanden entre la afición. Hasta Toché fue preguntado por ello en su balance del mercado y el director deportivo manchego fue claro: "Creo que es injusto achacar sólo al preparador físico las lesiones. Evidentemente nos preocupa, pero al final hay muchos factores que no podemos controlar y que menos puede controlar él". El Alba, que ya empezó la temporada con hasta siete bajas (Higinio, Puertas, Valverde, Capi, Villar, Agus Medina y Pacheco), sumó a Obeng en la primera jornada, a Rober González y San Bartolomé en la segunda y a Munir y Pepe Sánchez en la última. Las buenas noticias las han puesto las recuperaciones para la segunda jornada de Agus Medina, Pacheco y Villar, y la más que presumible vuelta, para esta jornada, de Higinio Marín a las convocatorias tras una temporada en blanco. A día hoy, la enfermería alberga a Obeng, que se perderá la temporada por una rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de su rodilla izquierda; Antonio Puertas, con idéntica lesión en su rodilla derecha que se produjo en abril; Víctor Valverde, que aguarda reincorporación pronto tras ser operado del menisco de su rodilla derecha también en abril; Higinio Marín, que todo parece indicar que volverá a las convocatorias esta semana; Capi, con una pubalgia que aún le hará perderse unas semanas de competición; Rober González, con un golpe que ya le privó de participar la pasada jornada; San Bartolomé y Pepe Sánchez, ambos con problemas musculares que les alejarán varias semanas de los terrenos de juego; y Munir, con una sobrecarga en su cuádriceps izquierdo que no le permitirá estar en Castellón. Una plaga de lesiones que se arrastra de temporadas anteriores y para la que el club, que siempre ha defendido que se trata de una cuestión multifactorial, sigue buscando soluciones. Lo cierto es que la preocupación ha ido creciendo y los resultados en este inicio de Liga, junto a las cinco nuevas bajas, han vuelto a encender las alarmas en el Carlos Belmonte.

images.caption: Obeng, tras ser operado de su lesión. ALBACETE BALOMPIÉ
Higinio, en el entrenamiento de este jueves. ALBACETE BALOMPIÉ

articles.title: Stefan Bajcetic: "A veces en la vida necesitas un cambio y pensar en ti y en tu familia"
articles.standfirst: El nuevo futbolista del Celta Fortuna se despidió con una carta de la afición del Liverpool
articles.summary: El nuevo futbolista del Celta Fortuna se despidió con una carta de la afición del Liverpool
articles.body: Stefan Bajcetic, que ha vuelto a Vigo para jugar inicialmente en el Celta Fortuna, se ha despedido con una carta abierta de la afición del Liverpool: "Estaba donde siempre quise estar. El amor que me han dado a lo largo de los cinco años que pasé en Liverpool ha sido increíble. Es fácil demostrar amor cuando las cosas van en la dirección correcta, pero no siempre ha sido mí caso y han estado ahí". Luché contra todas las lesiones y adversidades con la motivación de devolver el amor y la confianza que me mostraron durante este período, pero desafortunadamente no pude". Y explica su decisión: "A veces en la vida necesitas un cambio y pensar en ti y en tu familia. Creo que es el momento. Los recuerdos que tengo de este club se quedarán conmigo para siempre y me alegro de poder decirle a mis hijos que jugué en el mejor club de Inglaterra". Y lamenta lo que no pudo ser: "Nunca sabremos lo que podría haber sido, pero mi periodo allí me ha ayudado a madurar y crecer como persona y como jugador, desde lo que era cuando llegué a los 16 años hasta ahora que soy una persona completamente diferente".

images.caption: Bajcetic, con la presidenta Marián Mouriño en su regreso al Celta.

articles.title: Revuelo por Mike Dean: ''Me encanta, solíamos tener juegos''
articles.standfirst: El ex-colegiado de Premier, Mike Dean, ha hablado en un podcast inglés sobre los retos que se ponía durante los partidos
articles.summary: El ex-colegiado de Premier, Mike Dean, ha hablado en un podcast inglés sobre los retos que se ponía durante los partidos
articles.body: el pasado miércoles, en el podcast 'Jamie Vardy's Having A Party', el árbitro retirado, Mike Dean, declaró que se proponía juegos durante los partidos a modo de risa. Durante su aparición en el podcast del comediante Jamie Vardy, Mike Dean, ex-colegiado con experiencia internacional, confesaba que, previo a la creación del VAR, solía ver cuanto tiempo pasaba hasta usar el silbato durante algunos de los partidos que disputó en la Premier League. ''Estuvimos 20 o 25 minutos sin pitar un par de veces" confirmó. ''Me encanta, solíamos tener juegos'' explicaba Dean. ''Solía hacer otra cosa. Me quedaba en el círculo central, a ver cuánto tiempo podía seguir en el círculo central antes de tener que salir''. El inglés revelaba que intentaba correr dentro de las limitaciones del círculo central y que en una ocasión estuvo 15 minutos sin traspasarlas. Las declaraciones que afirmaba durante la charla ha causado gran revuelo en el mundo del fútbol inglés. ''Ha causado tanta controversia, y en todos mis años como árbitro profesional, nunca había escuchado nada sobre estos juegos, nunca'' decía Mark Halsey, árbitro de Premier League de 1999 a 2013. La actuación controversial de Mike no se limita a sus retos. Durante un partido que enfrentaba al Chelsea y al Tottenham, su trabajo destacó dentro del VAR. Dean se negó a mandar a su compañero a revisar varias acciones que suponían la expulsión del argentino Cuti Romero y la penalización de los defensas 'Spurs' por tirar del pelo a Marc Cucurella.

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of ‘smear campaign’ over Infantino, World Cup plan
articles.summary: UEFA seeks US testimony, documents for possible lawsuit; FIFA asks US court to defer or let it oppose UEFA’s request.
articles.body:
FIFA has accused UEFA of a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition” after European football’s governing body asked United States judges to force FIFA to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan.

Global football body FIFA’s divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped.

While FIFA quickly aborted the plans in response to the backlash, UEFA is now preparing possible legal action against FIFA President Gianni Infantino for alleged “criminal mismanagement”.

Last week, it filed requests in three US states seeking the disclosure of documents related to the plan from FIFA and partners, including prospective lead investor Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital firm.

If successful in gaining access to the documents, UEFA had said it intends to lodge a legal complaint in Switzerland, saying it has been assured the case would meet the requirements to be heard in a Swiss court.

But FIFA has hit back, asking US judges for permission to contest the UEFA requests.

“While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA’s smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” say the FIFA filings.

The filings say UEFA does not have the right to demand FIFA internal documents because no criminal proceedings yet exist in Switzerland or elsewhere.

Even if such proceedings did exist, the filings say, UEFA would not have legal standing because it has suffered no financial loss.

The FIFA filings also accuse UEFA of illegally bypassing Swiss courts but applying directly to US courts.

Disclosure of the documents, including correspondence involving Infantino and other named FIFA personnel and advisors, “would directly threaten FIFA’s interests and reveal sensitive and proprietary information”, say the filings.

UEFA has made no secret of its desire to remove Infantino, who had hoped to be re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next March after a highly successful World Cup.

UEFA may have been the harshest critic – it described his proposal as a “shady, opaque backroom deal” – but it has found solid support from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF).

CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino – UEFA’s Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out.

The three confederations have kept up the pressure and collaborated on a no-holds-barred joint letter issued on August 10.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held,” they wrote.

UEFA added: “FIFA must once again be governed as an institution serving football – not operate as an instrument of individual power.”

FIFA has repeatedly disputed those claims.

“This application is yet another step in UEFA’s smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” summarises one of the FIFA filings.

images.caption: FIFA President Gianni Infantino joins French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman at the Esports World Cup 2026 in Paris [Teresa Suarez/Reuters]

articles.title: Llorente ya tenía tomada la decisión antes del Mundial: "Era mi último momento con la Selección, pasará lo que pasará"
articles.summary: La Selección Española de Fútbol ha publicado un vídeo en sus redes acompañando a Marcos Llorente en el amanecer el día de la final del Mundial. Un momento especial en el que el jugador del Atlético tenía tomada la decisión de dejar la Selección pasara lo que pasara.
articles.body: La Selección Española de Fútbol ha publicado un vídeo en sus redes acompañando a Marcos Llorente en el amanecer el día de la final del Mundial. Un momento especial en el que el jugador del Atlético tenía tomada la decisión de dejar la Selección pasara lo que pasara. "Lo tenía ya pensado desde antes de venir. Mi último momento con la Selección, pasará lo que pasará. Creo que sí que es el momento de cerrar esta etapa que ha sido maravillosa, este último Mundial. No esperaba disfrutar tanto, quizás sabiendo que es la última vez que vas a estar aquí, la última vez que te vas a concentrar con la Selección, que vas a estar con estos compañeros. Creo que por mi vida, por mi familia, creo que es el momento de dar un paso al lado. Ojalá sea ganando. Después del Mundial, llamaré a Luis y le daré las gracias por haberme hecho campeón del mundo. Pero siento que es el momento de dejar esto a un lado", asegura en dicho vídeo Llorente.

articles.title: Watch 'Baby Gronk' Score 4 TDs, Total 250 Yards in Trending Videos from 8th Grade Debut
articles.summary: Madden San Miguel, also known as "Baby Gronk," recently made his eighth grade football debut.
articles.body:
Madden San Miguel, also known as "Baby Gronk," recently made his eighth grade football debut.

He revealed that he finished with 250 total yards and four touchdowns while posting multiple highlights from the game on social media.

He previously went viral in 2024 for announcing commitments to several colleges as an 11-year-old including Alabama, Georgia, Ohio State, Michigan, Florida, Nebraska and Tennessee.

Last year, Miguel reclassified from the class of 2032 to the 2031 class.

For now, he'll look to continue building momentum in eighth grade following a productive season debut.

articles.title: Richarlison omitted from Tottenham's Premier League squad
articles.summary: Richarlison may have played his last match for Tottenham after he was left out of the club's 25-man Premier League squad list on Thursday.Richarlison, who ha...
articles.body:
Richarlison may have played his last match for Tottenham after he was left out of the club's 25-man Premier League squad list on Thursday.

Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi, speaking following a 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle on Saturday, insisted Richarlison had "said too many times he wants to leave" and could bid farewell to the London club before the summer transfer window closed.

The Brazil forward released an incendiary social media post on Monday where he claimed "never again will anyone decide my future for me".

But talks over a potential return to Premier League rivals Everton, where he played from 2018 to 2022, stalled before Tuesday's 11:00 pm (2200 GMT) deadline in England.

Other transfer windows around the world remain open, however, and Trabzonspor have been linked with Richarlison ahead of Friday's deadline in Turkey.

Richarlison, who currently remains a Spurs player, made his feelings clear on Monday, with a remarkable outburst on Instagram.

"After everything I've been through in the last few years, I've decided that never again will anyone decide my future for me," he said.

"I went through a lot of bad things, and almost all of them happened because decisions were made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation –- none of that scares me. I've been through far worse, believe me.

"I've always made it clear, every time I had the chance, that leaving for another club would only happen if it was also good for the club. If it wasn't, I would never accept it. Just like I didn't accept it when everything was going badly and they needed me.

"I stayed and gave everything. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect I've always shown Spurs and everyone who worked with me during this period. Just don't try to decide for me."

The 29-year-old has struggled to make an impact at Tottenham since his move to north London four years ago.

Richarlison, who has been candid in the past about his mental health struggles, scored 12 goals during the 2025/26 campaign as Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation from the Premier League.

Spurs, despite spending more than £350 million ($473 million) in the summer transfer window, are bottom of the Premier League table after two games having been beaten 3-0 by Brentford in their season opener and then 2-0 at home to Newcastle.

articles.title: Two Stars Omitted From Liverpool Champions League Squad
articles.summary: Liverpool Champions League Squad Decision Leaves Chiesa and Endo Facing Uncertain FutureLiverpool have confirmed their squad for the league phase of the Cham...
articles.body:
Liverpool Champions League Squad Decision Leaves Chiesa and Endo Facing Uncertain Future

Liverpool have confirmed their squad for the league phase of the Champions League, and two familiar names are conspicuous by their absence.

As first reported by James Pearce of The Athletic , Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo have both been omitted from Andoni Iraola's 25-man group. Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike have been included despite continuing their rehabilitation from serious injuries.

For Chiesa and Endo, the decision feels significant. Liverpool have effectively provided an indication of where both players currently stand within Iraola's hierarchy.

Chiesa Pays Price for Liverpool's Summer Recruitment

Chiesa has missed Liverpool's opening two Premier League matches with a muscle problem and now faces the prospect of watching the Champions League campaign from outside the squad.

Pearce reports that the Italian "finds himself down the pecking order following the summer signings of wingers Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz."

Liverpool's recruitment has changed the landscape considerably.

Barcola represents a major investment, while Munoz provides another option across the attacking positions. Cody Gakpo remains at the club and Alexander Isak adds further firepower.

Chiesa therefore appears to have become collateral damage in Liverpool's reshaping of the attack.

Endo Omission Points Towards McConnell Opportunity

Perhaps more intriguing is the decision to exclude Endo.

The experienced midfielder was an unused substitute against both Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, with 22-year-old James McConnell preferred for Liverpool's European squad.

That feels like an important judgement from Iraola.

Endo has previously provided Liverpool with experience, discipline and a willingness to perform whatever role was required. Leaving him out while selecting McConnell suggests Liverpool are looking forward rather than relying upon past service.

It also creates a potentially significant opportunity for the academy graduate.

Liverpool Take Fitness Gamble on Injured Trio

Liverpool have adopted a different approach with Leoni, Bradley and Ekitike.

Pearce describes their inclusion as "welcome", with all three expected to return during the league phase.

Leoni is expected to resume training later this month after nearly a year recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury. Bradley has not played since suffering a serious knee injury against Arsenal in January, while Ekitike ruptured his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

Ekitike's inclusion is particularly noteworthy. The Frenchman finished last season as Liverpool's leading scorer with 17 goals and could provide Iraola with another major attacking weapon later in the competition.

Liverpool are effectively reserving places for players they believe can make a meaningful contribution once fit.

Champions League Squad Shows Iraola's Priorities

UEFA regulations require Liverpool to include at least eight "locally trained" players on List A, while younger players including Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni can be registered separately on List B.

That provides useful flexibility, although Liverpool's final selection remains revealing.

Chiesa and Endo are available senior players who have been deemed expendable for European purposes. Bradley, Leoni and Ekitike are injured players considered important enough to retain their places.

Squad lists can occasionally feel administrative. This one feels considerably more consequential.

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign against Atletico Madrid at Anfield next Wednesday. For those included, Europe offers another stage on which Iraola can begin shaping his Liverpool side.

For Chiesa and Endo, the message appears rather different.

There will understandably be frustration among Liverpool supporters when looking at these decisions, particularly after a summer in which questions have already been raised about the balance and depth of Iraola's squad.

Leaving Chiesa out feels logical given the arrival of Barcola and Munoz, although it also raises another question. What exactly is Liverpool's plan for the Italian now?

If he cannot command a Champions League place even while Ekitike remains sidelined, his route back towards meaningful first-team football appears increasingly narrow.

Endo's situation is arguably more surprising.

Liverpool supporters know his limitations, but they also know exactly what he offers. He provides experience, defensive awareness and reliability, qualities that can become extremely valuable during difficult European away matches.

Choosing McConnell instead represents a clear vote of confidence in youth. That should excite supporters, particularly those eager to see Liverpool provide genuine pathways for academy players.

The bigger concern surrounds Liverpool's injured contingent. Including Bradley, Leoni and Ekitike makes sense if their rehabilitation remains on schedule. Liverpool will desperately hope that all three return without setbacks.

Ekitike could be particularly important. A 17-goal striker returning during the league phase would effectively provide Iraola with another major attacking option midway through the campaign.

Ultimately, this squad feels like another indication that Liverpool are moving decisively into Iraola's era. Some established players are being pushed towards the margins, younger footballers are receiving opportunities and significant faith is being placed in recovering players.

Supporters will hope those calculations prove correct once the Champions League begins.

articles.title: Arsenal chief executive reveals 'dynasty' ambition
articles.summary: Arsenal are aiming to create a "dynasty" that will see them dominate European football, according to chief executive Richard Garlick."This is a period of dom...
articles.body:
Arsenal are aiming to create a "dynasty" that will see them dominate European football, according to chief executive Richard Garlick.

The Gunners won their first Premier League title in 22 years last season before suffering an agonising penalty shoot-out loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final.

Garlick, however, told the Men In Blazers Media Network that being crowned champions of England was only the beginning for the north London club.

"There was a moment where we enjoyed it, and you saw that enjoyment," he said.

"We are absolutely saying we're not done here. This is the start and not the end. We're at the start of something big. We want to push on and win more and more. It is absolutely trophies plural."

Arsenal have never won the Champions League or its predecessor, the European Cup.

They have, though, won their opening two games of the new Premier League campaign as they bid for the club's first back-to-back English top-tier titles since the 1930s.

"I dream of us being serial champions, of us repeating what we did last year and going one better maybe in the Champions League and winning major trophies," explained Garlick.

"This is a period of dominance, you could call it the start of a dynasty, this is what we're aiming to do.

"We're aiming to dominate football for the next few years on every front."

Arsenal face London rivals Chelsea, who've also won both their opening two Premier League games, at the Emirates on Sunday.

articles.title: ‘I spoke to him for 3 minutes’: José Mourinho reveals how he told Real Madrid star he was not in his plans
articles.summary: Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has provided an insight into the process which ultimately led to Dani Ceballos departing the club this summer.Midfielder...
articles.body:
Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has provided an insight into the process which ultimately led to Dani Ceballos departing the club this summer.

Midfielder Ceballos has of course seen his name reemerge front and centre in the Spanish media chatter over the last couple of days, after his long-awaited return to Real Betis was at last confirmed.

The one-time Arsenal man had spent the entire summer to that point as a free agent, following his departure from the aforementioned Real Madrid.

Despite his Blancos contract having still had a year to run, Ceballos agreed to a termination 12 months early. And as alluded to above, on Thursday, José Mourinho revealed the entirely straightforward manner in which this development came about.

Drawn on the name of his former midfielder during his pre-Real Betis press conference, the Portuguese tactician explained:

"Ceballos? I spoke to him for three minutes on the phone when I first got here. I told him he was not in my plans.

"A lot of times, players hold onto their contracts and say 'no, I want to stay', but Ceballos told me if I'm outside your plans, then I'd prefer to be free to decide my future, so he agreed to terminate his contract."

articles.title: Bay Area college football preview: Cal kick-starts Tosh Lupoi era with renewed rivalry game vs. UCLA
articles.summary: The Bears take on the Bruins in a showdown between QBs Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and Nico Iamaleava, while Stanford hosts ACC powerhouse Miami and San Jose St...
articles.body:
The Bears and the Bruins will meet for the 95th time in their storied 93-year-old West Coast rivalry, restoring Cal's tradition of the Joe Roth Memorial Game.

"It's important to me that the traditions here … and the knowledge of the greats like Joe, that our team is educated on those," first-year head coach Tosh Lupoi said at his Tuesday game week news conference, recounting the full presentation he and the program gave to the players to pass down Roth's legacy.

"If we had the majority of the team representing the principles and values of Joe Roth, we're probably going to be in a position to win a lot of games. Being the fighter, strong character, and embodying what a Cal Bear is all about."

And fitting of the legacy of one of the great quarterbacks in Cal football history, the battle between Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and UCLA 's Nico Iamaleava will be the main feature - with the two Polynesian quarterbacks looking to set the tone in what are anticipated to be pivotal seasons for both programs.

On the Bears' side, sophomore Sagapolutele is trying to build on a flashy freshman season in which he threw for 3,454 yards and 18 touchdowns. With Lupoi bringing in what was ranked (per 247 Sports) as the 14th-best transfer portal cadre in the nation, and with Cal Athletics receiving a record $88.5 million in donations over the last year, the Bears step onto the field with new excitement and raised expectations.

On the Bruins' end, Iamaleava looks to bounce back after a disappointing first season in Los Angeles in which his team finished 3-9. Though it is debatable how much of the blame of UCLA's troubles last year falls on Iamaleava, there is pressure on the senior to lift the program out of its mediocrity, especially after his tumultuous exit from Tennessee a year prior. Like Lupoi, UCLA coach Bob Chesney will also make his coaching debut after an offseason in which he brought in 43 transfers along with 17 incoming freshmen.

The stakes are about as high as they can get for a season opener between two non-ranked teams. There is newness, there is history, anticipation and pressure. All of which will play out before what is expected to be a sold-out Memorial Stadium crowd.

Roth was an All-American QB for the Bears in 1975-76, who died of melanoma shortly after his second season; his jersey No. 12 remains the only one retired by the program. Cal will don its classic royal-blue Joe Roth jerseys and yellow helmets when they kick off their season at 7:30 p.m. PT.

Stanford welcomes national championship runner-ups: After notching new head coach Tavita Pritchard's first victory in their 37-27 win over Hawai'i in Week 0, the Cardinal will immediately face their toughest challenge of the season when the No. 7 Miami Hurricanes enter Stanford Stadium. Fresh off a playoff run that brought the Hurricanes one drive from winning a national championship, coach Mario Cristobal and his squad look to kick-start their road back up the mountain after reloading with one of the best transfer portal classes.

"Excited about this upcoming week because it is another week to learn about ourselves and where we can continue to grow against an outstanding opponent," Pritchard told reporters at his Monday presser.

The Stanford defense will look to limit quarterback Darian Mensah , the transfer now guiding the Miami offense after leading Duke to an ACC title last season, throwing for 3,973 passing yards and 34 touchdowns. Star sophomore wide receiver Malachi Toney will also pose problems for the Cardinal with his speed and versatility. The Hurricanes move Toney all across the formation, whether in the slot, in motion, or sometimes even in the backfield, which is how he earned a First-Team All-ACC honor in his freshman season last year.

On the other side of the ball, Stanford's new starting quarterback Davis Warren will try to follow up on his strong debut, in which he completed 22 of 34 passes for 310 yards and a touchdown. That might prove difficult for the sixth-year Michigan transfer going up against the talent of the Hurricanes' defense. Miami defensive linemen Ahmad Moten and Justin Scott will pose problems for a beat-up Stanford offensive line that will be without starting center Aiden Kilstrom, who suffered a lower-extremity injury in Week 0. Additionally, Stanford's starting right tackle Niki Prongos and guard Simone Pele are listed as questionable.

Stanford will take on the ACC title favorites under the Friday night lights at 6 p.m. PST.

Spartans look to bounce back: San Jose State heads to Eastern Michigan after a 42-26 loss to the No. 15 USC Trojans in Week 0.

Though the Spartans found themselves trailing 28-0 at halftime in the Coliseum, they found some encouraging signs in their 23-point fourth quarter, albeit achieving that against the Trojans' backups. New QB Luke Weaver led three touchdown drives for San Jose, completing 21 of 32 passes for 234 yards and two touchdowns on the night, to go along with 42 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown.

"Eastern Michigan's got a lot of confidence (after) a really good win in their first game. They're home, the momentum of winning - everything is going sky-high right now," Spartans coach Ken Niumatalolo told reporters Wednesday. The Eagles defeated Sacramento State 28-17 in their Week 0 win.

"We just got to make sure we prepare the best way we can. You go from playing USC, who everybody knows about them. Sometimes, the human nature side of it, people will look at social media and different things and (won't) give Eastern Michigan the respect they deserve. And also, we're San Jose State. We're not Ohio State or anybody, so we got to get ready for a battle against a team that won their first game."

Kenzo Fukuda is a freelance journalist born and raised in San Francisco. He has covered the Giants, Warriors and Valkyries since 2025, and previously covered Cal football and women's basketball from 2022-24. You can follow him on X at @kenzofuku.

articles.summary: Going into Europe with our boysIn two weeks, we kick off our UEFA Europa League campaign with an away match in Sofia. We will go into the tournament with the...
articles.body:
In two weeks, we kick off our UEFA Europa League campaign with an away match in Sofia. We will go into the tournament with the following 27-man squad:

Tickets for our UEFA Europa League home matches are now available on open sale in the form of four-game packages.

How the league phase in the UEFA Europa League works

A league format has replaced the group stage in UEFA competitions for the past few years. In the UEFA Europa League, just like in the Champions League, each team is drawn against eight different opponents, playing four home and four away matches.

At the end of the eight rounds, an overall table is formed for all 36 participating teams . The top eight teams then advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing 9th to 24th compete in a play-off round with home and away legs for the remaining knockout stage spots.

Further changes compared to the previous format: after elimination, there is no longer any relegation to the UEFA Conference League, as was previously the case for third-placed teams in the group stage. Additionally, the league now runs until the end of January.

articles.title: North Carolina GM Michael Lombardi reportedly resigns in wake of internal investigation
articles.summary: Lombardi came to UNC with Bill Belichick.
articles.body:
Michael Lombardi has resigned at North Carolina.

The team's general manager had been on leave as the result of an internal investigation. Thursday, ESPN reported that the former NFL front office executive had stepped down from his position

Lombardi came to North Carolina with Bill Belichick when the former New England Patriots coach was hired after the 2024 season. Lombardi famously said that North Carolina would consider itself a 33rd NFL franchise, but the program struggled in 2025 and went 4-8.

Lombardi was placed on paid administrative leave in late July after an ex-UNC employee reportedly filed an HR complaint.

His resignation comes less than a week after his attorney told the Athletic that the investigation was a "witch hunt."

"If UNC had grounds to fire Michael for cause, they wouldn't need to conduct such a far-ranging, lengthy witch hunt. They would have done so by now," attorney Tom Mars said. "I think the motive behind the investigation goes further than a $1.5 million buyout. After all, UNC could fire Michael (or the athletic director or any head coach) for no reason at all just by paying their buyout. In today's world, $1.5 million is just a drop in the bucket, so there must be other reasons behind this multimillion-dollar investigation."

Lombardi's salary of $1.5 million made him the highest-paid GM in college football.

articles.title: Radu firma el empate del Celta en Anoeta
articles.standfirst: El portero del equipo vigués evitó el tanto de la Real con varias muy buenas paradas en la primera parte, con una segunda más igualada pero sin que el marcador se moviera
articles.summary: El portero del equipo vigués evitó el tanto de la Real con varias muy buenas paradas en la primera parte, con una segunda más igualada pero sin que el marcador se moviera
articles.body: Real Sociedad y Celta empataron a cero en Anoeta, en el partido adelantado de la sexta jornada, por coincidir con la primera de una Europa League en la que participan ambos equipos. Radu evitó el gol de los locales en la primera parte y en la segunda el partido se equilibró, pero sin acertar a marcar ningún futbolista. El partido comenzó con imprecisiones de Real y Celta, sin ocasiones claras hasta que Jon Martín cabeceó picado un córner sacado en corto y obligó a Radu a meter una buena mano para evitar el primer tanto, no encontrando luego rematador un centro de Oyarzabal, en su primera aparición en el área rival. La segunda provocó otra gran parada del portero del conjunto celeste a un zudazo, cayéndole el rechace a Kubo, que mandó la pelota a las nubes. El equipo ayer dirigido por John Maisano, tras la sanción a Pellegrino Matarazzo por su roja ante el Espanyol, estaba haciendo méritos para tomar ventaja en el marcador y los aumentó con un chut potente de Yangel Herrera ajustado al palo que no se coló por otra mano brillante del cancerbero rumano. Hubo que esperar al minuto 40 para ver peligro del Celta, al sacarse Ilaix Moriba un zurdazo que se fue por poco por arriba de la portería del ex internacional. La Real volvió al ataque después del paso por los vestuarios, pero en una contra el equipo vigués desaprovechó un tres contra dos, rematando fuera Antañón. El debutante se quedó con ganas de tener una segunda opción, tras una internada de Carreira con la pelota no llegando a sus pies porque Turrientes metió una de las suyas. Los locales reaccionaron con una cabalgada de Oyarzabal, a la que siguió una acción de Kubo, al que Marcos Alonso tuvo que derribar al borde del área, para que no fuera a más. Maisano y Giraldez movieron sus banquillos y las entradas de Pablo Durán, Iago Aspas y Driouets se notaron más, ya que los gallegos tuvieron más balón que hasta entonces, aunque Guedes pidió penalti al poco de entrar el encuentro por los txuriurdin. Aspas pudo ser el héroe una vez más, pero su remate forzado lo detuvo Remiro. Guedes insistió con un derechazo que se le marchó desviado y la Real terminó con hasta cuatro córners seguidos, pero sin marcar y, por lo tanto, no moviéndose el resultado inicial.
